cards.question: What are the King's College criteria for liver transplantation in paracetamol-induced ALF?
cards.answer: Arterial pH <7.30 after resuscitation, OR all three of: PT >100 s (INR >6.5), creatinine >300 µmol/L, and grade III/IV encephalopathy. These inform prognosis and specialist listing assessment, not automatic eligibility. Discuss acute liver injury/ALF with a liver unit early; do not wait for criteria.

cards.question: How is raised intracranial pressure managed in acute liver failure?
cards.answer: Aim for serum sodium 145–155 mmol/L with hypertonic saline, head-up 30°, mannitol or hypertonic saline boluses for surges, mild hypothermia (35–36 °C) if refractory, and avoid hypotonic fluids and hypercapnia.

cards.question: When is N-acetylcysteine indicated in non-paracetamol ALF?
cards.answer: Lee et al. (2009) studied a 72-hour NAC infusion in adults with non-paracetamol ALF. Overall survival was not significantly improved; transplant-free survival benefit was concentrated in grade I–II encephalopathy. Discuss use and duration with a liver centre; the trial does not establish a completed 21-hour paracetamol course as the non-paracetamol regimen.
